correctness.rationale: On labelled bidirected cycles stable sets are independent dominating sets. The cyclic membership language excludes 11 and 000 in each coordinate, so the trace counts each labelled ordered pair once with target-symbol XOR weight. Independently used a 9-state pair automaton (age of the last occupied site in each coordinate); exact determinant, length-one and length-two corrections, and two dominant-root derivatives all agree. Replay: python3 /workspace/audit-04-reproduce.py (SymPy); no frozen script was executed. At t=1 the one-coordinate recurrent shift has cycles of lengths 2 and 3 and is irreducible, hence primitive, as is its tensor square. Analytic isolation of its simple Perron root gives a uniform exponentially small trace error near t=1; differentiating and substituting the centered characteristic-function argument proves the stated moments and Gaussian limit, with strictly positive exact variance. For odd n the sole agreement vertex cannot be in both sets (its neighbors would also have to agree), so an alternating path with that one uncovered vertex gives precisely 2n possibilities; even n has the two proper alternating assignments. These arguments include n=3 and use ordered, not rotation-quotiented, pairs.
